result:
None of your Revisit dates have passed yet. The next one is bake-to-order on 2 Dec 2026.

I've left out the free first box and the plain 50% off first month, because you dropped both on 6 Oct 2026. Only 6 of the 52 free boxes became paying subscribers, and they used Saturday slots that paying customers wanted. The free box only comes back if paid signups fall below 8 a month for 2 months in a row. October had 15, so you're well above that.

**1. Referral offer from your current subscribers**
Your ledger allows one exception: 50% off the first month is worth testing if the new person comes through a referral from an existing subscriber. Give each of your 140 subscribers a personal code or card for their next box. The friend gets 50% off their first month, and the subscriber gets something cheap for you, like a pastry or a small loaf added to their box. Run it for 6 weeks. Then compare how many referred people stay after the first month with the 6 out of 52 from the free box. People who come through a friend usually stick around better than people who came for something free. This test is how you'd find out.

**2. A paid one-off box you collect at the shop**
Some people won't commit to a subscription before they've tasted the bread. Offer a single box with no subscription, paid at €18 or close to it, and collected at the shop on Saturday. Since they collect it, it doesn't use any of your Saturday delivery slots, and because it's paid it doesn't break your no-free-trial decision. It still fits bake-to-order: people order by the 6 pm cutoff the day before. When they collect, hand them a card that puts what they paid toward a subscription if they sign up within 2 weeks. Count how many of these buyers convert. That tells you if not wanting to commit is what's holding people back.

**3. Get the bread in front of people at local shops**
Find 2 or 3 places within your 3 km area where your future customers already go, like a cheese shop, a deli or a coffee bar. Supply them a couple of loaves a week to serve or sell, with a small sign and a QR code to subscribe. Bake these loaves to order for the partners so you don't end up with daily surplus stock. The loaves, signs and printing should fit inside your €300 a month. Give each partner its own QR code so you can see which one brings in signups. After 2 months, keep the ones that work.

I'd start with #1. It costs the least, your ledger already allows it, and the result answers whether a discount can work at all.

When you pick one, tell me and I'll log it in the ledger with what you set aside and why.
